bluf: Amsive is a US mid market performance agency selling audience data (Audience Science, Xact Data Platform), digital media, SEO and AEO alongside in house direct mail and print. Its record shows an award cycle in motion: Search Engine Land 2025 Agency of the Year for SEO, an AEO expansion in 2026-03, Amsive Health formalized in 2026-01 and a commissioned Forrester study in 2026-07 claiming 134% ROI. The record points it toward AI search and financial and healthcare verticals. What a rival should know: it sells AI visibility with no llms.txt and no audited AI visibility product on record, and 13 of its 14 clients are names with no described work.
doing:
The positioning line reads: data led performance agency joining audience intelligence (Audience Science), digital media, SEO and AEO with in house direct mail and print. In plain words: media and search on top of a proprietary audience data layer, plus physical production. The headline claim, a commissioned Forrester Total Economic Impact study, credits its audience led approach with 134% ROI over three years and, in the 2026-07 release, 40% annual customer growth; commissioned, so a claim.

Service lines run from Audience Science and Data & Analytics through paid media, retail media, SEO and AEO, influencer, direct mail and email to web development and print; Audience Science and the Xact Data Platform are the proprietary products and Google Premier Partner the only partner named. It leads with Data & Measurement and SEO, both scored 3: the homepage hero is Audience Science plus the Forrester TEI, and the SEO line carries the 2025 Search Engine Land award, seven subservice pages and Lily Ray, VP of SEO and AI Search, leading research. Core lines scored 2 are AI Search (a dedicated AEO/GEO/LLMO page), Email & CRM (with a Redwood Credit Union email lift case), Paid Search and Web & Product (Shopify, BigCommerce and Adobe Commerce builds). Paid social, programmatic, retail media, creator, CRO, local and B2B score 1 with no evidence note.

Its AI posture: AEO as an extension of the SEO practice plus AI enhanced execution and AI enabled creative; no agent or automation product shows in the record.

Moves in order: 2025-01 a leadership succession; 2025-03 Google Premier Partner again; 2025-11 the Search Engine Land award plus best enterprise SEO initiative for MSN; 2026-01 Amsive Health formalized for health plans, systems and providers; 2026-02 two Search Engine Land Awards; 2026-03 answer engine optimization added; 2026-07 the Forrester study. No pricing model, no case study with described work, no jobs, offices, employee count or owner: all absent from the record.
clients:
The stated client type is mid market. The record lists verticals spanning banks and credit unions, insurance, healthcare and Medicare Advantage, consumer finance and mortgage, higher education, wine and spirits, senior living, retail and consumer goods, ecommerce and B2B, and the home market is the US with no offices listed.

The needs read holds 14 clients, one observed and 13 named only. The observed one is MSN, whose need reads as organic demand from the award entry for best overall SEO initiative, enterprise, at the 2025 Search Engine Land Awards. The rest are case study pages that name the client and nothing about the work: Commerce Bank, Delta Community Credit Union, Redwood Credit Union, Redwood Credit Union Insurance Services, Hiscox, OppLoans, University of Tennessee, Keene State College, Emergient and Vermont Blue Advantage, Christian Care Ministry and Globe Bag Co., plus VOSS Water and Roscato Wine as slugs only. For all 13 the need is inferred from what Amsive leads with, SEO and data and measurement, and the record says so. One partial exception: the Email & CRM evidence note cites a Redwood Credit Union email lift case, a CRM and owned audiences signal the needs table does not carry.

The shared list is empty: no client on this record appears on another tracked agency's book.

What the base needs next is a judgment with low confidence, because 13 of 14 engagements show no described work. The book leans to financial services and higher education, where KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) makes AI search visibility measurement the likely next ask, and KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer) makes first party data inputs to platform automation likely, which is where Audience Science already sits.
house:
Three say and do tests on amsive.com. AI Search / GEO is contradicted: it sells AI visibility and publishes no llms.txt. Paid Search is corroborated: 42 Google ads in the Transparency Center, 39 in the last 30 days, last shown 2026-09-26; a sample reads: Data-led strategy, audience-led development, reliable direct mail production + tracking. Publishing cadence is corroborated: the sitemap lists 771 URLs, 67 updated in 90 days and 287 in 365. Integrity reads 66.7.

The one flagged gap is that missing llms.txt. No AI crawlers are blocked. The stack is GTM and Osano on WordPress; the record detects no social pixels, test tools or ABM stack. LinkedIn shows 24+ ads on the first results page, 23 company page and 1 thought leader, and the note calls the count a floor; a sample reads: 52% of recent switchers compare plans every year, versus 24% of members who have never switched. Meta and TikTok: the record is silent.
market:
Horus reads a tailwind index of 16.4, band Favored. Best placed for KJ4, the platforms are absorbing the execution layer (net 0.19, driven by Data & Measurement), and KJ1, the click is being replaced by the citation (net 0.152, AI Search / GEO). Most exposed to KJ5, the price of attention splits in two (net minus 0.059, on Paid Social and Programmatic & CTV), and KJ6, the agency middle is being hollowed out. The mix sits at 17:00 on the Solar Arc, dusk; best fit is The Walled Oasis at 44/100. It is making P4 (supply the inputs automation runs on) and P7 (owned audience hedges), partial on P1 (audited AI visibility), absent on P2, P3, P6 and P8, unknown on P5.

The Monsoon read is 57.1, Onshore wind, migration 54.6 against displacement 59.6, with SEO (12) and Web & Product (8) carrying the most movable hours. Shore: 65% South and Southeast Asia, 25% Latin America. The footprint is inferred with no hub office listed; the one onshore claim, in its own words, is in house direct mail and print.
openings:
The strongest opening is the AI visibility contradiction: answer engine optimization added in 2026-03, no llms.txt on its own house, no audited AI visibility product in the record (P1 partial). A rival that leads with an audited citation number is likely to win that conversation, moderate confidence. Falsifier: an llms.txt on amsive.com or a published AI visibility scorecard would close it.

Second, the book is contestable because it is opaque: 13 of 14 clients are names with no described work, so the bank, credit union and higher education accounts are a question to ask; roughly even chance any given one is loose, low confidence. Third, with no public pricing (P5 unknown), a transparent outcome priced offer is a conversation it cannot have in public. Fourth, P2 is absent, no feed, schema or entity work on core search and web lines, unclaimed ground for a rival selling the machine readable layer; P8 is absent too, no ads tested inside AI assistants. No price opening is computed: displacement reads 59.6 and print and mail are onshore in its own words, so an offshore undercut is unlikely to bite beyond the SEO and web hours the Monsoon read marks movable.
watch: Indicator I7, holiday 2026 agentic checkout volume and merchant opt out rates, reads December 2026 to January 2027: high Shopify opt out rates would slow KJ4, the judgment Amsive is best placed for.

Indicator I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, reads late October 2026: search and other growth below 10% flags cannibalization and would sharpen the KJ1 tailwind behind its AEO line.
Indicator I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, reads late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.
Indicator I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, is rolling: pricing below $20 CPM signals supply outrunning demand in the assistant ad market it is absent from on P8.
Follow up the 2026-03 AEO expansion and the 2026-07 Forrester study: an audited AI visibility product or an llms.txt on amsive.com would flip the P1 read and close the strongest opening.
